crime_highlights: Mr. Paul walked to his vehicle, retrieved a 9 mm. semi-automatic hand gun and returned to the party area
The man fell to the ground, shot in the face.
He shot one twice in the back and once in the jaw, another in the forehead, and another in the right eye.
All three men were killed by the shots.
Mr. Paul shot him twice in the arm from a distance of about 10 feet.
rationale_highlights: This information does help to shed light on Mr. Paul's aboriginal community and his connection to that community.
appropriately reflects both Mr. Paul's relatively young age and his aboriginal status, absent which a longer period may well have been imposed
note: Appeal court; sentencing judge's own Gladue weighing is in para 26 (too long).

crime_highlights: Under the age of 14 years, T.G. could not consent in law, and therefore any sexual activity with D.G. was an assault.
T.G. became pregnant when she was 13 years old, giving birth when she was 14 years old and D.G. was 20 years old.
The two lived together as husband and wife for several years after the birth of their son
rationale_highlights: By failing to consider D.G.'s background, and weigh it when assessing his moral blameworthiness, the sentencing judge committed another error.
He did not, however, weigh this background or any of the individual circumstances of D.G.'s upbringing when he fixed the sentence.
The historic and individual circumstances of an Aboriginal offender are highly relevant to the assessment of moral blameworthiness--an assessment that cried out to be performed in this case
note: Appeal court; offender history from Gladue report is in paras 27 and 31.

crime_highlights: the appellant committed aggravated assault by using a knife to slash the face of an acquaintance
the appellant approached him, slashed his face, and walked away
required emergency surgery and was left with lasting damage to his facial nerves
rationale_highlights: including serious childhood neglect and abuse, and substance abuse, related to his very disadvantaged upbringing
representation by counsel that there were significant Gladue factors
He found the Gladue factors, the mitigating factor of the guilty pleas, and the prospects of rehabilitation all to be relevant.
note: Appeal only about pre-sentence credit; Gladue effect on sentence never clearly stated.
